desc:
A sorted array of distinct integers was cut at some position into a front part and a back part and the two parts were swapped, producing nums (a cut at the very start or end leaves it unchanged).

Given nums and an integer x, return the value in nums that is closest to x, that is, the one minimising |value - x|. If two values are equally close, return the smaller one. For nums = [6, 7, 9, 1, 3, 4]: x = 5 gives 4 (4 and 6 tie, take 4), x = 8 gives 7, and x = 100 gives 9. Use O(log n) time.
constraints: nums is a rotation of a sorted array
hints: In a sorted array, the closest value is one of the two neighbours of the position where x would be inserted.
Locate the start s of the sorted order (the minimum). Then you can treat nums[(s + j) % n] as a sorted array indexed by j.
Binary search the first virtual position j with value at least x. Compare the values at j - 1 and j (when they exist); on a tie in distance keep the smaller value, which is the one at j - 1.
editorial: First find the start s of the sorted order with the 'compare with nums[hi]' binary search. Then perform a lower-bound search on virtual indices: the first j such that nums[(s + j) % n] ≥ x (or n if none).

The closest value must be one of the two neighbours of that insertion point: the value just before it (largest below x) and the value at it (smallest not below x). If j == 0 or j == n only one candidate exists. Otherwise compute the two distances and return the lower one; on equal distance return the smaller value, i.e. the one at j - 1. Two O(log n) searches, O(1) space.
